title: the Yaksha's questions
hook: a deer runs off with a brahmin's fire-sticks, the brothers chase it into thirst, and a voice at a lake says: answer first
carry: a brother who didn't wait to hear them

segments.voice: Yesterday: vara, a boon. Savitri talked with Death until he gave Satyavan back, and they walked home through the dark. Your line was a walk home through the dark.

A pair of fire-sticks, swinging from a deer's antlers. A brahmin comes running to the Pandavas in their forest exile. He had left his arani, the two pieces of wood he rubs together to kindle his sacred fire, hanging on a tree. A deer rubbed against the tree, the sticks caught in its antlers, and now it's bounding away with them. Without them, he can't keep his fire. The five brothers take up their bows and go after it, deeper into the trees than any of them meant to go.
screen: `FIRE-STICKS ON A DEER'S ANTLERS.` → `A BRAHMIN'S FIRE AT STAKE.` → `FIVE BROTHERS GIVE CHASE.`

segments.voice: The deer stays just out of reach. The brothers shoot and miss, chase and fall behind, and then it's simply gone. They sink down under a tree, exhausted and parched, and the talk turns sour. Nakula asks why trouble keeps finding a family that has tried to live rightly. One by one the brothers remember the dice hall and what they failed to do there. Yudhishthira says only that misfortune has no limits, and no one can say where it comes from. Then he turns practical. Nakula, he says, climb that tree and look for water. Nakula sees green plants and cranes, the signs of water not far off, and goes alone to bring some back. He finds a lake, clear and still. He is about to drink when a voice speaks from nowhere. Don't be rash, child. This lake is mine. Answer my questions first, then drink and take as much as you like. Nakula is burning with thirst. He doesn't stop. He kneels, drinks, and falls down dead on the bank. So the episode begins not with a riddle but with a duty, brothers running after someone else's fire. And its crisis is a plain temptation: water to a thirsty man, and one voice asking him to pause first. The questions haven't been asked yet.
screen: `A CHASE THAT COMES TO NOTHING.` · `NAKULA CLIMBS AND SEES CRANES.` · `THIS LAKE IS MINE. ANSWER FIRST.` · then, large: `HE DRINKS, AND FALLS.`

segments.voice: If there's a glass of water near you, set it where you can see it, or simply picture one waiting, the way the lake waited in front of Nakula. Breathe in and ask one plain question, what do I actually need right now, then breathe out and listen, without hurrying the answer. If you pray, you can offer that pause in your prayer.
Arani, the fire-sticks a brahmin lost when a deer carried them off into the trees. A voice at a lake that asks before it lets anyone drink, and a brother too thirsty to listen. Today's word.
Your line: a brother who didn't wait to hear them. The lake asked first; the thirst answered. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: The Yaksha's questions are a dialogue on dharma set in the Pandavas' forest years, and the episode opens with the brothers' chase to recover a brahmin's fire-sticks.

chat.says: Why did Nakula die at the lake? Was the water poisoned?
options: No. A voice asked him to answer questions first, and he drank without listening.
Yes. The brothers' enemies had poisoned the lake to trap them in the forest.
He fell because he drank far too fast after chasing the deer all day.
chat.meaning: The voice said: this lake is mine, answer my questions first. Nakula was burning with thirst, drank without listening, and fell.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Aranyaka Parva), the episode of the Yaksha's questions: the brahmin's arani carried off by a deer; the chase; the brothers' talk under the tree; Nakula at the lake

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: the brahmin's arani hung on a tree and caught in a deer's antlers; the chase fails; under the tree Nakula asks why misfortune comes to the virtuous, and the brothers recall the dice hall; Yudhishthira's reply on misfortune.
Confirm Nakula climbs a tree and sees water plants and cranes, and the voice's words (the lake is mine; answer first, then drink and take).
Original: अरणि; confirm spelling and stress. Some editions call the episode Aranya rather than Vana Parva.
